title: The God Object (Bloated Abstraction)
pattern: A single struct representing a massive conceptual space with dozens of unrelated responsibilities, fields, and helper methods.
why_bad: It is a massive failure of decomposition. It results in extremely high coupling, making the codebase highly fragile. Any change to a minor configuration parameter ripples and risks breaking unrelated socket or user database logic.
detection: A struct declaration with an exceptionally high number of fields (e.g., 10 or more) or public methods (e.g., 20 or more) that span different functional domains.
counterexample: None. Large, monolithic abstractions always indicate a design error.
fix: Decompose the God Object into smaller, cohesive, deep structs based on the Single Responsibility Principle, and coordinate them via simple interfaces.
source: Martin Fowler, *Refactoring* (1999), Chapter 3 ("Large Class"); John K. Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design* (2018).
